cases.prompt: Write a libFuzzer dictionary for our HTTP/1.1 request parser and show how to use it.

all.why: includes method tokens as quoted strings

expectations: The dictionary lists one quoted token per line (methods, header names, "HTTP/1.1") with # comments grouping them.
Non-printable bytes such as CRLF are written as escapes (\r\n or \x0D\x0A).
Entries are short atomic tokens rather than whole requests, and the list stays focused.

cases.prompt: Our file format starts with the bytes 89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A. Add that to a dictionary and run AFL++ with it.

all.why: writes the magic with hex escapes
passes the dictionary to afl-fuzz with -x

expectations: Writes the signature as a hex-escaped quoted string such as "\x89PNG\x0D\x0A\x1A\x0A".
